newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil poised to enter Yankee bond market.
newsitem.headline: Brazil poised to enter Yankee bond market.

text.p: Brazil filed a shelf registration with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on Wednesday to issue up to $5.0 billion in debt in what market sources said was a bid to establish a yield curve in the Yankee bond market.
"The Yankee market is not popular among Brazilian issuers so the government wants to open it up and set up a yield curve in the U.S.," said a Eurobond trader at a large international bank in Brazil.

Brazil has been working on the shelf registration for over a year. The Central Bank last year said it would initially launch a token $10 million Yankee issue to help open the market for Brazilian corporates and state-owned firms.
But traders said the government would probably opt for a larger issue of about $700 million with a minimum 10-year maturity to establish a true benchmark in the U.S. market.
Central Bank officials were not immediately available for comment on the shelf registration.
already announced intentions to issue a $300 million Yankee bond sometime this year. That deal, however, was expected to follow a sovereign issue.
Up to now, the Republic of Brazil and Brazilian corporates have concentrated on the Eurobond market, which is governed by less stringent securities regulations.
